description: A 4HP four-into-one stereo mixer with a level knob and a level CV per section, and a left and right mix output

params.text: Sets the level of the whole mix, 0% fully counter-clockwise to 200% fully clockwise, at 100% in the centre
Sets that section's level, 0% fully counter-clockwise to 200% fully clockwise, at 100% in the centre
Passes the level CV of the section above down to this one while it is green, and blocks it while it is red

inputs.text: Moves the level of the whole mix; 5V here adds 100%, and the total is held between 0% and 200%
Moves that section's level; 5V here adds 100%, and the total is held between 0% and 200%
The left side of that stereo section; with its right jack empty this signal goes to both sides unless mono-to-stereo is turned off
The right side of that stereo section; an empty jack reads the left jack of the same section while mono-to-stereo is on

outputs.text: Carries the left sides of the four sections at their levels, divided by how many are patched in averaging mode, then taken through the master knob
Carries the right sides of the four sections at their levels, divided by how many are patched in averaging mode, then taken through the master knob

notes: a green light between a section's two input jacks means its left signal is copied to the right when the right jack is empty; the light turns red when that is switched off
there are no per-section outputs on this one, only the left and right mix
menu: Mix mode: Averaging mix, Unity mix — divides the total by the number of patched inputs, or leaves it a plain sum; the light by the MIX output is dark for averaging, red for unity
Mono-to-Stereo (L>R) — turned off, a section with only its left jack patched contributes nothing to the right mix
A-amplification, B-amplification, C-amplification, D-amplification: Normal, Inverted — flips the sign of that section's contribution, and lights a small red mark beside its knob
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
